method: Static PE/code/data-flow review; no sample execution or C2 contact. Sandbox pages were inaccessible.

evidence: PE entry 0x402674 calls main 0x401cb0. Its mode branches reach DLL extraction, service hijack, Active Setup installation, injection, and shell cleanup.

At 0x401260 the installer constructs a system-directory DLL path, opens HKLM SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters, deletes ServiceDLL at 0x401320 and writes the replacement at 0x40133e.
0x402460 finds resource type DLL/id 101, loads and locks its bytes, then 0x4023c0 creates the destination and writes them. The embedded PE starts at file offset 0x5060.

0x401150 builds a target path for Internet Explorer, Notepad or Calculator. It creates the child, allocates remote memory, writes the DLL pathname, resolves kernel32!LoadLibraryA, and passes that function and the remote pathname to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.
0x401900 generates an Active Setup GUID subkey, sets StubPath at 0x401a4b, reads its own image through CRT streams, patches the copied configuration, writes it, and launches the copy.
0x401390 gets its current short pathname, reads COMSPEC, constructs /c del with the current image path, and starts the cleanup process.
StormServer.dll, Storm ddos Server, the welcome banner and embedded Storm ddos DNS/STORM packet format corroborate identity. No ransomware behavior or Remcos attribution was established.
samples.limits: Reconstructed-memory-style image with resolved IAT values and extensive zeroed embedded code. Surviving installer paths establish hostile purpose; no claim that this damaged artifact successfully runs or that the missing DDoS loop was recovered.

samples.identification: Lold Update Client HTTP task implant
samples.marker: Lold HTTP task implant: detect ghosted image context rewrite
evidence: Manifest names Lold.UpdateClient and a patchable .loldcfg configuration holds an HTTP server URL, access key, polling state and paths masquerading as Microsoft SyncServices/OneDrive components.
0x23a19f9f780 sends a JSON heartbeat to /files/hb/<id>.json, lists /files?prefix=inbox/<id>/, retrieves task JSON from /files/inbox/, parses op and dispatches ping, exec, sleep, fetch and uninstall.

The exec branch parses cmd at 0x23a19fa0105 and calls 0x23a19fa1760 at 0x23a19fa014a. That helper converts the received command, prepends UTF-16 cmd.exe /C at 0x23a19fa18a7, and passes the buffer to CreateProcessW at 0x23a19fa1947 with CREATE_NO_WINDOW.

0x23a19fa5ae1 installs CommandLineTemplate and name properties in a CommandLineEventConsumer through helper 0x23a19fa9fc0. Other installation paths construct timer/event filters and __FilterToConsumerBinding for durable reactivation.
Payload management supports manifest/chunk acquisition and reconstruction, disk launch and ghosted image launch. These are code paths, not an assertion that a payload was acquired during this review.

0x23a19fbd9f0 obtains a temporary file, passes TRUE and FileDispositionInformation=13 to NtSetInformationFile at 0x23a19fbda49, writes payload bytes through NtWriteFile, creates SEC_IMAGE through NtCreateSection at 0x23a19fbdae4 and closes the delete-pending file.
0x23a19fc0460 maps the resulting section into the child with NtMapViewOfSection at 0x23a19fc04d1, calls the context helper at 0x23a19fc0540, then ResumeThread at 0x23a19fc0569.

0x23a19fc0e20 adds the mapped image base to its parsed entry RVA, writes x64 CONTEXT.Rcx (or WOW64 Eax) and calls SetThreadContext at 0x23a19fc0eed. It also updates the child image-base field through WriteProcessMemory at 0x23a19fc0fb3.
MicrosoftEdgeUpdateTask_ is a selected task-name prefix; it does not establish a reference to the browser name MicrosoftEdge.
samples.limits: Static tracing only. The embedded server was not contacted and payload bytes were not fetched. No unsupported Cobalt Strike, IcedID, njRAT, Satacom or Stealc attribution was adopted.

samples.marker: PStore autorun worm: exclude autorun directive from API trait
evidence: PE32 with populated UPX0, low entropy and no declared imports is an unpacked-memory-style artifact retaining its UPX entry stub; failed stock decompression does not mean its code is absent.

0x428653 repeatedly obtains the string length, XORs each byte with the supplied key and writes it back. Call sites supply keys including 2 and 5. Data contains both already-decoded strings and remaining encoded strings.

Representative recovery: XOR2 Amlvglv/V{rg8... becomes Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded; XOR5 UJVQ% v%MQQU*4+4 becomes POST %s HTTP/1.1; XOR7 @bsWuhdFccubtt becomes GetProcAddress; XOR2 Ycwvmpwl_ becomes [autorun].

0x42a20c repeatedly enumerates drive roots C through X, calls drive classification at 0x42a2b1, requires DRIVE_REMOVABLE=2, constructs root executable and autorun.inf destinations, copies the installed self image at 0x42a2f4, marks it hidden/system (attributes 6), and writes [autorun] plus ShellExecute=autorun.exe through CRT output calls at 0x42a377 and 0x42a3a1.

0x42a4d4 loads pstorec.dll and resolves PStoreCreateInstance at 0x42a506. COM helpers invoke EnumTypes (+0x38), EnumSubtypes (+0x3c), EnumItems (+0x54), and ReadItem (+0x44). It collects pass_sites and auto_complete_pass credentials.
Report helper 0x42a48e formats source/name/password records and appends them to a global report buffer at 0x401000. 0x42acc8 returns that report.
The reporting loop calls 0x42acc8 at 0x42b07b, encodes its returned buffer at 0x42b0bf, incorporates it into the outgoing form body, and calls HTTP transport 0x42964e at 0x42b13a.

0x42964e resolves the HTTP host, connects TCP port 80, builds the POST request with the form body at 0x42977f, and sends it at 0x4297ba. This is an actual credential-report-to-send path, not API co-occurrence.

Other code establishes Run/Winlogon registry changes and downloads/launches server-selected executable URLs. The existing three hostile traits already capture the independently proven worm and credential theft results.
ShellExecute=autorun.exe is an AutoRun configuration directive. It is not evidence of a ShellExecute Windows API import, lookup or call.
samples.limits: No ransomware behavior was established. Memory-image damage and retained packing scaffolding prevent assuming ordinary standalone execution, but surviving propagation and credential-report-to-send code establish the artifact's malicious purpose.
